levels.note: formulaone L0 (client-ssh cast on the drifter host, port 2232): /formulaone/formulaone0.c is a byte-at-a-time password oracle - send 'Password: ', read_byte() recv's ONE byte per PASSWD[i] comparison; a wrong byte breaks the loop and answers 'WRONG PASSWORD', a correct byte makes the daemon BLOCK in recv for the next byte. The solve: probe(prefix) classifies each candidate byte (WRONG / BLOCKED=correct), sweeping 62 chars x 32 positions -> 'U6pyn4b5DVhJdbyTD7fOBlnyxkSozcTQ' built incrementally (pos 0 -> U ... pos 31 -> full), then a fresh connection sends the password, dup2's the socket to stdio and system('/bin/sh') runs id + cat /etc/formulaone_pass/formulaone0 -> U6pyn4b5DVhJdbyTD7fOBlnyxkSozcTQ. levels.note: formulaone L2 (client-ssh cast on the drifter host, port 2232): the setuid binary invents /tmp/tmp_XXXX names (26^4 = 456976 possibilities), requires stat(name)!=0 (the name must NOT exist), then fopen(name,'r') and cats it. levels.note: formulaone3 (setuid, no canary) maps a SysV shm segment SHM_EXEC (RWX) and does a DOUBLE READ of echo->sz: load #1 for the sz<=0xff check, load #2 for the memcpy size, with the puts() call between them. We own the segment (created 0777 before the run); a toggler flips sz between 10 and 0x400 so the check passes while memcpy smears 1KB of our data over the stack (sz=0x400 stays inside the 8KB shm - 0x2000 would fault mid-copy and never return). The payload sets doecho's saved EIP (buf+0x110 <- shm+0x114) to shellcode inside the RWX shm (ret2shm; GNU_STACK is RW so the stack itself is not executable). The shm VA is deterministic with ASLR off; a mimic probe (same shmget/shmat in a plain process) gave 0x7ffff7fb5000 and a 4KB sweep around that region hit the true base at 0xf7fb9000. GOTCHA: strtoul('ADC00ADC',0,0) parses base-0 as DECIMAL and fails - pass 0xADC00ADC or the attacker creates key 0 while the binary uses its own segment (silent no-op).
